purpose: Collapse three drifted password-policy implementations into the one in strong-password.validator.ts, and give that policy the unit tests it never had. The shared validator enforced no upper length bound while the two private copies in gekta-registration.service.ts and password-reset.service.ts capped at 128, so a 240-character password was accepted at registration and refused at reset; the copies in turn never applied the all-same and sequential checks. Verified empirically by running the real code, not by reading it.
requiredInvariants: The consolidated policy is the union of the rules the three implementations already enforced between them - no rule is invented and none is dropped.
Each service keeps its own error code and exception type; only the predicate moves to the shared validator.

The character-class rule stays. ASVS V6.2.5 asks for it to be removed, but only together with a breached-password check, which is blocked on an owner decision about third-party list licensing - removing it alone would weaken the policy rather than modernise it.
No existing account can be locked out: this policy runs when a password is set, never when one is verified.

Tightening registration with the 128 cap matches what the product already enforced everywhere else - the register form caps at maxLength 128 and the reset flow rejected above 128 - so only a direct API call could previously set a longer password.
No production, REG.RU, DNS or database mutation.
acceptance: grep for the duplicated 'classes < 3' rule finds it only in strong-password.validator.ts.
strong-password.validator.spec.ts covers both sides of every rule, including the 240-character password the split policy disagreed about.
The src/modules/auth and src/common/validators suites pass with no regressions.
